# Dunia Alerts

> Live early warnings for schools in Nairobi, Kenya. Dunia Alerts watches air quality (PM2.5), heat, heavy rain and river flow around pilot schools, up to 48 hours ahead. A person on the Dunia team checks each warning and sends the head teacher one clear step; parents are told in English and Kiswahili. Every response is timed and recorded for the pilot report. A Dunia Endelevu pilot, led by Alana Chelangat, starting in 2026.

- [About Dunia Alerts](https://alerts.duniaendelevu.org/about): the problem, how it works, data sources, status, and how to support or partner
- [Live dashboard](https://alerts.duniaendelevu.org/): the working tool (records are kept on the Dunia team's device)
- [Classroom screen](https://alerts.duniaendelevu.org/classroom?demo=1): the wall screen for classrooms, shown here with example data
- [Dunia Endelevu](https://duniaendelevu.org/): the youth-led climate organisation that runs the pilot
- [Alana Chelangat](https://alanachelangat.com/): founder of Dunia Endelevu

## Facts

- Hazards and alert levels: PM2.5 of 35.5 µg/m³ or more (US EPA 2024 "unhealthy for sensitive groups"); 30 mm or more of rain in a day; a high of 30 °C or more; a river at twice its usual flow.
- Data: Open-Meteo weather forecasts; Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service air quality; Global Flood Awareness System river flow; OpenAQ ground sensors (including AirQo) when connected.
- A person always decides before a warning is sent. No children's names are recorded. Free for schools.
- Classroom screen: shows a classroom's temperature, fresh air (CO₂), dust (PM2.5) and humidity from an indoor sensor, plus the weather and air outside, in English and Kiswahili. Built; indoor sensors are the next step, with funding.
- Status: built and live; pilot schools being added; results will be published openly. There are no pilot results yet.
